Standard: Lanyards, wires, hoses, and store umbilicals are of the correct length for routing and can be secured and retained for all carriage and release operating conditions. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Analyze models or drawings for proper routing (e.g., correct length, bend radius, clamp and retention points) and security of all lanyards, wires, hoses, and umbilicals for all applicable weapon stations and mixed load configurations. If lanyard routing is significantly different than previous cleared, then endurance testing IAW MIL-HDBK-1763, Test 253, is required. Demonstration.
  (1) Verify routing and security of all lanyards, wires, hoses, and umbilicals for all weapon stations and mixed load configurations. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Verify correct function and release of all arming lanyards, retention lanyards, pull-out switches, and store umbilicals IAW MIL-HDBK-1763, Test 110. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (2) Flight test: Lanyard and umbilical continues to function and is not damaged when exposed to carriage environments. For expendable stores, verify that lanyards and umbilicals safely separate as intended during store release sequences and the air vehicle retains all hardware designated for retention. Flight test footage enables observation of lanyards and umbilicals during flight to identify snags, chafing, stowage, or retention issues.
